notes:
Lead came from self-serve signup (free credits used). Early discovery call 2026-02-25. Brightline is building an in-app support assistant (SaaS) for SMB customers. Primary needs: streaming chat for low-latency responses, tool/function-calling to execute account lookups and ticket creation, and reliable structured output (JSON mode) for downstream ingestion. They are on Node.js backend and started with hosted API. Reported issues: streaming responses sometimes deliver partial JSON chunks that break their parser; function calling schema mismatch — tool 'create_ticket' expects 'priority' enum but their frontend sends string labels; sometimes function_call.name is null when calling with set of candidate tools; errors reproducible in our hosted-alpha region but not in local mock. They tried toggling "JSON mode" in SDK with no consistent fix.

- 2026-02-20: self-serve signup, used free credits, initial test integration (node sdk) — basic chat success.

- "We see malformed JSON about 2-3x per 1k streams — enough to break our parser and cause fallbacks to non-structured flow."
- "Function call sometimes returns without name — then frontend can't map to tool handler."

Technical notes / current hypotheses:
- Streaming chunk boundaries may split JSON objects; client-side reassembly logic in their node SDK may not be robust to partial messages.
- Function schema definitions sent in calls include mixed types (number vs string) for the same field across examples — leads to runtime validation failures.
- There may be an SDK bug in our Node helper that strips function_call.name when a tool list is long or when descriptions contain special chars.
